subject: Intermittent silent completions reported by BrightBridge — triage findings
messages:
From: Alex Soto <alex@brightbridge.ai>
To: support@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:12:15 -0700
Subject: Intermittent silent completions from Redwood API

Hi team,

We're seeing a handful of API calls return an empty/blank text output (HTTP 200 with zero-length completion) over the last 24 hours. This is impacting an internal workflow where we parse the assistant's JSON output — the parser sees an empty string and fails downstream.

Examples (request ids attached):
- req_20270302_01a3b (2027-03-02T02:03:21Z)
- req_20270302_04d2f (2027-03-02T05:11:09Z)

I grabbed a short screencap and exported the raw request IDs and timestamps (attached). No 500s in our telemetry, just the successful response body being empty. Can you confirm whether this is a platform issue?

Thanks,
Alex Soto
SRE, BrightBridge AI
Attachments: request_ids.txt (text), screencap_0302.mp4 (video)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Soto <alex@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 10:01:32 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent silent completions from Redwood API

Hi Alex — thanks for the report and for attaching the IDs. We're looking into this now. I've looped in Marcus (SRE) to run through backend logs and Monica from Customer Success for any product-side context.

Quick ask while we triage: can you also share one full raw request payload (with prompt and headers) for one of the failing IDs and the exact response body you received? If you prefer, you can drop it into the Drive link you provided.

We'll confirm whether this is a platform-side regression or a client-side fallback/edge case and get back within 24 hours.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | support@redwood.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Alex Soto <alex@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 11:18:04 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent silent completions from Redwood API

On Wed, Mar 3, 2027 at 11:18 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Alex — thanks for the report...

Thanks for flagging this, Alex. I pulled service-side telemetry covering the timestamps from the attached request_ids and ran them through the request tracing pipeline. Summary of findings:

- For the two example request IDs you provided, Redwood's front-end accepted the requests and routed them to a GPU serving group. There were no 5xx errors, HTTP status returned was 200 in our logs.
- The model runtime returned an empty payload in both cases (response body size = 0 bytes) according to the payload metadata we emit. However, I could not find any corresponding runtime exceptions or host OOM events in the serving container logs.
- No network disconnects were recorded between the serving layer and the API gateway for those traces.
- We reproduced a similar shape in a controlled replay with the same prompt length and temperature on the same model variant, but our replay produced normal non-empty output in 30/30 attempts.

Initial interpretation: either (A) something in the client-side HTTP pipeline stripped/trimmed the body after successful response, or (B) a very narrow race condition where the runtime emitted an empty payload without logging an error (rare).

Next steps I took:
- Requested expanded low-level runtime logs for the serving hosts that handled the two traces (attached partial log extract: request_logs_0302.csv).
- Ran a stress replay with identical headers/payload and observed no reproductions.

Action items for BrightBridge: please provide one full raw HTTP exchange (request + full response bytes as captured on your side) for any failing ID. That will let us determine if the response body was actually empty when it left Redwood or if it was dropped in transit/client.

If you can't share the raw exchange, Monica and I recommend enabling request-level tracing on a sample route (we can give you a short configuration snippet) so that if this recurs we capture the full wire bytes and a span id.

Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: request_logs_0302.csv (partial log extract)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Soto <alex@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent silent completions from Redwood API — triage & closure

Hi Alex — quick closure note from our side after the triage run.

We were unable to reproduce the silent/empty completions using the request payloads and timings you provided. Service telemetry for the timestamps you reported shows successful 200 responses; the payload metadata indicates non-empty sizes for the majority of requests in that window. The few traces that showed zero-size payload metadata did not surface any runtime exceptions or platform-level failures.

Given:
- Internal replay succeeded consistently (30/30)
- No platform errors (5xx, OOM, host reboots) in the relevant cluster windows
- No network anomalies between API gateway and serving tier in our logs

Conclusion: we cannot confirm a Redwood platform defect at this time. Possible causes still include client-side HTTP handling or an edge caching/proxy that trimmed the body.

Please do one of the following if you see this again and want us to re-open an investigation:
- Share a raw HTTP capture (request + response bytes) for an affected request id, or
- Enable request-level tracing using the snippet Marcus provided and share the span ids.

Monica is available to help with the tracing config and to review client-side networking. If BrightBridge prefers, we can schedule a short joint debug session to capture a live reproduction.

If you prefer us to keep the ticket open for 72 hours while you change client telemetry, tell us and we'll keep monitoring. Otherwise we'll close this incident on our side.

Thanks — appreciate the detailed examples, and let us know how you'd like to proceed.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
